sections.section_title: How to Regard Apostles -- Servants, Stewards, and the Lord's Judgment
sections.summary: Paul defines apostles as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries, argues that faithfulness is the sole criterion for stewards, disclaims the competence of any human court to judge him, and directs the Corinthians to wait for the Lord's coming when hidden motives will be revealed and each will receive commendation from God.

sections.section_title: The Application Revealed -- Not Beyond What Is Written
sections.summary: Paul reveals he has been using himself and Apollos as pedagogical illustrations, commands the Corinthians not to exceed scriptural principles in their evaluations, and asks the devastating question: 'What do you have that you did not receive? If then you received it, why do you boast as if you did not receive it?'

sections.section_title: The Ironic Contrast -- The Corinthians' Self-Satisfaction and the Apostles' Suffering
sections.summary: Paul deploys sustained irony to contrast the Corinthians' self-image as satiated, rich, and reigning with the apostles' actual condition of hunger, homelessness, abuse, and treatment as the scum of the world, exposing their premature realized eschatology.

sections.section_title: The Father's Appeal and the Sending of Timothy
sections.summary: Paul shifts from irony to paternal appeal, identifying himself as the Corinthians' father through the gospel, urging them to imitate his cruciform pattern of life, and announcing that he is sending Timothy to remind them of his ways in Christ.

sections.section_title: Warning to the Arrogant -- Words versus Power
sections.summary: Paul warns the arrogant that he is coming personally and will test not their words but their power, because the kingdom of God consists not in talk but in power, and asks whether they want him to come with a rod of discipline or with love and gentleness.
